EXTRA CLASS · PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY

Every place in town, with its lesson on the card.

The town-map class: twenty-eight places walk the whole town in tour order — the places that teach us, the places that keep us safe, the food-and-shopping run, the quiet squares, the ways the town moves and the green places — and every lesson below is a kid-followable guide, right on this page.

HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Every place in town — with a lesson on its card.

The Places in the Community class is a bonus class, kept beside the main learning path like the Kitchen Helper and the Doctor Visit: the regular classes stay the core sequence, and this one is for the days when somebody asks what is that building? Twenty-eight places a town is made of — the library, the fire station, the bakery, the bus stop, the park — each one on its own card, and each card opens a simple lesson a kid can follow: what the place is, who works there, what we do there, step by step, and one way to play it at home tonight.

The places run in tour order on purpose. The learning places come first, because school is the building your child already owns; then the helping places, where doctors, dentists and the two stations keep everyone safe; then the food-and-shopping run; the quiet squares that make a town work; the ways the town moves; and the last group is the fresh air — gardens, parks, playgrounds, the zoo. By the end, the whole map of the town sits in one deck of cards.

THE PLACES, SIX WALKS OF TOWN

Twenty-eight cards, six kinds of places.

Twenty-eight places in six groups, in the order a real trip across town unfolds. Every lesson is right here on this page — the original card beside the kid-followable guide, family after family.

THE CLASS GAME

The Town Walk: build a street on the floor.

Stack the cards face down. Draw the top one, place it at the end of a growing "street" across the floor, and say what happens there — at the bakery, I buy bread! At the fire station, the truck sleeps! Card by card the street grows around the room until all twenty-eight places stand in a row, and then comes the best part: walk the whole town, end to end, and greet every stop on the way. Grown-ups walk it too — the losing shoe and the wrong turn are all part of the map.

SAME PLACE, TWO NAMES

Movie theater and cinema. Both are right.

Places travel even less than games do — the building never moves, but its name crosses the ocean and changes clothes. This class says so out loud. The cinema is the movie theater; the pharmacy is the drugstore or the chemist’s; the gas station sells petrol across the ocean; the dentist’s office is the dentist’s surgery in the UK; the sports center plays as the leisure centre; the shopping cart is a trolley; the garbage and trash are the rubbish; the street box is a mailbox or a post box; the pet shop is a pet store; and the airplane flies as the aeroplane. Whichever your family says, your child hears both — and learns early that places, like words, come in kinds.

Age ranges are a guide, not a test. Start with the places your child already loves, follow the questions, follow the child — and before any real visit, pull the matching card and read its lesson together: a place that is half-familiar before you arrive is a friend, not a stranger.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 28 cards in Places in the Community, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Places in the Community. We have 28 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. Cards 1–10
  3. 02
    Card 1 · School

    “School! Here is where we learn our letters and our numbers, paint pictures and make friends. The clock on top tells everyone when the school day starts — and when it is time to come home!”

    How: Play "what comes next": morning carpet, story time, snack, play outside. Line up three toys as a school day and walk a small figure through it — the routine is the lesson.

  4. 03
    Card 2 · Library

    “The library! Shh — here are a thousand books waiting. We pick some, we read them at home, and we bring them back so the next child can borrow them. The open book on the building shows everyone: stories live here!”

    How: Play library at home: line up books on a couch cushion, make a paper "library card", and take turns being the librarian who stamps the returns. Borrowing and bringing back is the whole game.

  5. 04
    Card 3 · Museum

    “The museum! Inside are old and wonderful things — bones of giant animals, paintings, rockets! We look with our eyes, we walk with quiet feet, and we say ‘wow‘ as many times as we want.”

    How: Open a home museum: three treasures on a table (a shiny stone, an old key, a feather), paper tickets, and a tour guide who tells one story about each thing. Guides get very dramatic — let them.

  6. 05
    Card 4 · Cinema

    “The cinema! We pick our film, we find our seat, the lights go down — hush — and the picture begins, bigger than anything at home! When it ends, the lights come up and we all clap a little.”

    How: Home cinema night: dim the lamps, line up the chairs, tickets torn from paper, popcorn in cups. Someone plays the "trailer" by telling tomorrow’s story in a big voice. Lights down, film on.

  7. 06
    Card 5 · Hospital

    “The hospital! When someone is hurt or very unwell, we come here, and doctors and nurses know exactly what to do. See the cross on the building? It means: helpers inside!”

    How: Treat every toy in the room: one teddy with a sore paw, one dolly with a cough. Bandage with toilet paper, listen with a cardboard-tube stethoscope, and finish every visit with a sticker — hospitals always have stickers.

  8. 07
    Card 6 · Dentist’s Office

    “The dentist’s office! The dentist counts our teeth — one, two, three — looks for sugar bugs, and polishes until everything shines. Open wide and say ahh! Brave visits get a sticker from the treasure box.”

    How: Play dentist with a doll: count all the teeth out loud (grown-ups have up to 32!), check with a spoon for a mirror, and brush every single one with an actual toothbrush. The counting IS the check-up practice.

  9. 08
    Card 7 · Pharmacy

    “The pharmacy! The pharmacist takes the paper from the doctor and gives us the medicine that makes us better. Medicine comes from here — and only grown-ups carry it home.”

    How: Sort the "medicine shelf": colored pom-poms in pill bottles by color and size, labels drawn on, one rule repeated kindly — medicine is only for grown-ups to give. Sorting practice wearing a pharmacist’s coat.

  10. 09
    Card 8 · Fire Station

    “The fire station! The firefighters eat, sleep and wait right here — and when the bell rings, WHOOSH, down the pole, on with the boots, and the big red truck roars out to help!”

    How: Bell rings, boots on: someone rings an imaginary bell, and the firefighter must put on shoes, hat and "backpack" and run to the door — timed, cheering, again. Ready-in-a-hurry is the game and the real skill.

  11. 10
    Card 9 · Police Station

    “The police station! Police officers keep everyone safe — they help lost children find their grown-ups, they direct traffic, and they work while the whole town sleeps. The star on the badge means: I help!”

    How: Play the friendly-offer game: one toy walks a "street" of cushions and gets lost, and the officer helps by asking questions — what is your name, who are we looking for? Practicing name-and-grown-up is real safety drills in a game.

  12. 11
    Card 10 · Supermarket

    “The supermarket! We take a cart — some say a trolley — and we fill it with the food for our week. Apples, bread, milk, cheese... what goes in YOUR basket? And at the end, the beeping: beep, beep, beep — all paid!”

    How: Make a picture shopping list together — five drawings, five finds. Your child holds the list, hunts the shelves, and crosses off every match. The trip stops being "waiting" and becomes a quest.

  13. Cards 11–20
  14. 12
    Card 11 · Bakery

    “The bakery! Smell that? The baker woke up SO early to bake the bread. We point at what we want — one bun, please! — it goes in the paper bag, still warm, and it never survives the walk home.”

    How: Bakery shop at home: play-dough rolls, a paper apron, and customers who order by count — "three buns, please!" Counting out the order is the math; the paper bag is the theater.

  15. 13
    Card 12 · Farmers’ Market

    “The farmers’ market! The farmers bring what they grew — carrots with the green tops still on, corn, berries! We meet the grower, we taste a sample, and the food was in the ground this week.”

    How: Market morning game: lay fruits and vegetables on a blanket, assign a farmer and a shopper, and trade with play coins. The farmer must name every crop and answer one question about it ("how do carrots grow?").

  16. 14
    Card 13 · Restaurant

    “The restaurant! We sit, we read the menu, we ORDER — ‘pasta, please!‘ — and then the waiter brings it, hot from the kitchen. At the end we say thank you, and we do not wash a single dish!”

    How: Paper-menu restaurant tonight: draw tonight’s dinner as a menu with pictures, take the order with a notepad, serve with a folded towel over the arm. The waiter role is the prize — fight over who gets it.

  17. 15
    Card 14 · Pet Shop

    “The pet shop! Look — fish, hamsters, a dog in the window and a cat on a cushion! Every animal here needs food, a bed and a kind family. We can visit the window any day — looking is free.”

    How: Pet shop vet day: every stuffed animal in the house goes to the shop for a check-up — weighed, fed a pretend snack, given a paper collar. Then the shop opens and the customer picks a pet to "adopt" — with a promise to feed it forever.

  18. 16
    Card 15 · Bank

    “The bank! Grown-ups keep their money here so it is safe. The money machine — the ATM — waits outside, and it gives the right coins any time, day or night. Inside, very big doors keep everything protected.”

    How: Play bank with a cereal-box teller window: deposits of buttons, withdrawals for "groceries", a receipt scribbled on paper. The piggy bank is the home branch — count the savings, make a deposit, watch it grow.

  19. 17
    Card 16 · Post Office

    “The post office! We write a card, the post officer weighs it — ploop on the scale — we press on a stamp, and off it goes, truck, train, plane, all the way to Grandma’s door!”

    How: The full mail loop at home: write a real letter to someone in the house, stamp it with stickers, deliver it through a door-slot or under a pillow, and wait for the reply. Sending AND receiving — both halves are magic.

  20. 18
    Card 17 · Hair Salon

    “The hair salon! We climb into the big chair, the cape goes on — whoosh — the wash is warm and bubbly, and then: snip, snip, snip! The mirror shows the new haircut, and we say thank you very much!”

    How: Salon day for the dolls: a towel cape, a spray bottle wash, a pretend trim, and the all-important mirror reveal with a gasp of admiration. The stylist narrates like an artist — "and NOW... the big finish!"

  21. 19
    Card 18 · Hotel

    “The hotel! Travelers sleep here when they are far from home. We check in at the desk, we get a key card — beep! — and there is our room: a bed, a window, and tiny bottles of shampoo. Breakfast downstairs!”

    How: Home hotel: a suitcase packed for one night in the living room, paper keys handed over the "front desk", room service ( crackers and juice ) ordered by phone. Check out by 11, as the sign says.

  22. 20
    Card 19 · Gas Station

    “The gas station! The car is hungry — glug, glug, glug — we feed it gas from the pump, clean the windshield — squeak, squeak — and pay inside. Sometimes the driver of the car gets a snack too!”

    How: Car wash and fill-up for ride-ons: chalk prices on paper, a "pump" that counts to ten while filling, windshield wiped with a real cloth. Ten is the magic number — every fill-up is a counting exercise.

  23. 21
    Card 20 · Bus Stop

    “The bus stop! We check the time, we wait on the bench, and down the street — here it comes, the big bus! We wave, we climb on, we tap our card, and the driver says good morning. Beep!”

    How: Bus route around the house: chairs in a line, tickets torn from paper, stops called at the fridge (Stop 1: Kitchen), the bookshelf (Stop 2: Library) and the bathroom (Stop 3: Splash Pools). Driver rotates every lap.

  24. Cards 21–28
  25. 22
    Card 21 · Train Station

    “The train station! We check the big board — platform 2! — we stand behind the yellow line, and HERE IT COMES: whoooosh, the doors slide open, and off we ride, clickety-clack, clickety-clack!”

    How: Station at home: the sofa is platform 1, tickets punched with a hole punch, the conductor calls "all aboard!" and clips every ticket. Leave exactly on time — the clock on the card is the boss, and the train waits for nobody.

  26. 23
    Card 22 · Airport

    “The airport! Suitcases roll, the tower watches the sky, and the airplane takes off — vrrrooom, up up and away! We check in, we wave at the planes, and one day we climb the stairs and fly somewhere wonderful ourselves.”

    How: Front-row plane spotting: many airports have a viewing spot where the jets land right over your head. Score each landing, guess the destination from the colors, and practice the wave — every pilot appreciates it.

  27. 24
    Card 23 · Community Garden

    “The community garden! Everyone in the neighborhood grows something here — carrots, beans, strawberries. We water, we weed a little, we wait... and one day, the very first tomato. Grown by US!”

    How: Claim a window box as the family plot: plant radishes or beans (fast, forgiving, exciting to pull up), water on a schedule, and measure the sprout with a paper ruler every Sunday. The wait is the lesson.

  28. 25
    Card 24 · Park

    “The park! Run on the grass, lie under the big tree, listen to the leaves — shhh, shhh. Bring a ball, feed exactly zero pigeons (they prefer it), and rest on the bench with a cold drink. Fresh air is the whole plan.”

    How: Meet-a-tree day: pick one tree, learn its bark by hand and its leaves by shape, and visit it every season — spring buds, summer shade, autumn colors, winter branches. One tree makes the whole park personal.

  29. 26
    Card 25 · Playground

    “The playground! Up the ladder — step, step, step — sit at the top... and WHEEE, down the slide! Then the swings: lean back, pump the legs, higher, higher! The playground is where the wiggles go to be used up.”

    How: Playground circuit: one trip on each thing, then choose a favorite and do it three more times. Teach the two big rules kindly — one at a time on the slide, and wait for the swing to stop before you grab it.

  30. 27
    Card 26 · Recycling Center

    “The recycling center! Bottles HERE, paper THERE, cardboard in the middle — crash, clink, stomp! The arrows mean: this is not garbage, this is tomorrow’s something new.”

    How: Home sorting line: three boxes for paper, plastic and cans, and a "quality inspector" who checks each item and stamps it through. The inspector role rotates — and the sorting habit sticks for life.

  31. 28
    Card 27 · Sports Center

    “The sports center! Inside there is a pool, a court, a gym — every game lives here, even when it rains. Bring your shoes, bring your water bottle, and try something new: swimming today, maybe badminton next week!”

    How: Family mini-olympics on any flat floor: sock-ball toss into laundry baskets, hallway bowling, a balance-beam line of tape, medal ceremony at the end (paper medals, national anthem optional, absolutely sung).

  32. 29
    Card 28 · Zoo

    “The zoo! Today we visit the whole world in one walk — the lions, the penguins, the tall tall giraffes! Quiet voices, walking feet, and look who is awake today... every animal has a name plate; we read them together!”

    How: Pick three animals before you go — one big, one small, one with a funny name — and make them the quest. Read each name plate out loud: where it lives, what it eats. Three real facts beat a rushed lap of everything.

  33. 30
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  34. 31
    Check

    “Can you find School? Now show me Bank.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  35. 32
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 28 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
